newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FAXON, FROST, GAYDOS SHARE LEAD, TIGER WOODS SURGES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FAXON, FROST, GAYDOS SHARE LEAD, TIGER WOODS SURGES.

text.p: Brad Faxon, David Frost and Paul Goydos shared the second-round lead and tied the 36-hole tournament record at the MasterCard Colonial Friday, but the most noise was made by Tiger Woods.
The 21-year-old Masters champ fired a five-under-par 30 on the back nine en route to a second-day 65 and a 132 total to pull within three shots of the leaders going into the weekend rounds.

Woods is seeking his third PGA Tour victory in as many starts, but it appeared he might be out of the picture as he came to the 10th tee trailing the leaders by eight shots. But just as he has done so many times in his young career, Woods put on a spirited back-nine rally.
He birdied holes 10, 11, 13, 17 and 18, closing with a 20-foot birdie putt to the delight of the huge galleries.
"Something just clicked in, it's hard to explain," Woods said. "I picked up ground today. My goal is to pick up ground every day and be in contention on the back nine on Sunday."
Faxon entered the day with a one-shot lead after an opening score of 63. He followed that with a 67, making birdies on holes one, seven, nine, 11, 14 and 15.
That made up for bogeys on holes three and five and gave hime an 11-under-par total of 129, tying the tournament record set by Fulton Allem in 1993.
"I didn't hit it as good today as on Thursday, but the course is there for the taking," Faxon said. "I made birdies on holes when I hit it in the fairway."
During his stop in the media room after his second round, Faxon chided Woods for saying he was winning without his best play. Woods responded that he was simply telling the truth.
"I played really well at the Masters and won. You saw the way I played last week (in a win at the Byron Nelson) and in the first two rounds, it's just not the same."
After his round, Woods put in an extended session on the practice putting green, working on his stroke with personal instructor Butch Harmon.

South African David Frost made the biggest move of the day with a seven-under 63 at Colonial Country Club on a muggy Friday. He began the second round three shots behind Faxon, but birdied holes one, two, seven, 10 through 12 and 18.
"I putted well and hit it better today," Frost said. "The course was playing hard and fast and I had to be careful out there."

Goydos, who won for the first time last year, fired a 65 after opening the tournament with a 64. He birdied holes two, three, six and seven for a 31 on the front nine. He added a birdie on the par-five 11th hole.
"This is probably the lowest opening rounds I've had in my career," Goydos said. "If I shoot 22-under, then I think I'll win."
Justin Leonard, who lives 30 miles to the east in Dallas, was in a threesome tied for fourth, two shots behind the leaders. Also in the group were Jim Furyk and Bob Tway.
Weather forecasts for the weekend called for a good chance of rain both days, leaving players uncertain of what conditions they will face.
"It all depends on if we get rain," Woods said. "This course can be very hard, if the wind blows."
